questions.q: What keyboard shortcut opens Chrome DevTools directly to the Console tab?
options: F12 (or Ctrl+Shift+J on Windows)
Ctrl+Alt+Delete
Alt+F4
Ctrl+Shift+Esc
questions.explain: F12 or Ctrl+Shift+J opens Chrome DevTools directly to the Console tab.

questions.q: Why is console.table specifically useful for blockchain-related debugging?
options: It renders an array of objects as an actual table, which matches the shape most blockchain data (lists of transactions, balances) comes in
It is the only console method that works with numbers
It automatically connects to a blockchain node
It replaces the need for console.log entirely
questions.explain: Arrays of objects are exactly the shape of most blockchain data, and console.table renders that shape far more readably than nested braces.

questions.q: What makes console.error different from console.log in a real browser console?
options: It's styled in red and comes with a clickable stack trace showing exactly which line logged it
console.error cannot accept a string argument
console.error only works inside Node.js, never in a browser
There is no actual difference between the two
questions.explain: console.error visually distinguishes error-level messages and includes a stack trace for tracing the source.

questions.q: What can you do with the console beyond just reading logged messages?
options: Type and run JavaScript expressions live, directly against the actual open page, and see the result immediately
Only view messages — it has no interactive input of any kind
Edit the page's HTML file directly on disk
Send network requests but never run arbitrary JavaScript
questions.explain: The console includes a live prompt that executes JavaScript against the running page, not just a read-only log viewer.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the core debugging habit the console enables?
options: Checking what a value actually is at a given point, instead of assuming what it should be
Deleting console.log statements before testing any code
Avoiding the console entirely in favor of guessing
Only using the console after a script has already crashed
questions.explain: Adding a console.log before a suspicious line and checking the real value against the assumed value resolves most bugs.
